# 2 Baruch Chapter 15 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** First Fast and Vision

---

**15:1** And the Lord answered and said to me: "You have asked me concerning the multitude of good things which have passed away from the world and of what salvation shall come.

**15:2** As regards the things of which you spoke, there is destined for this world a recompense in its own time; but the promise of the life to come shall not be moved.

**15:3** For this world is to the Most High a trouble and weariness only; but the world to come is a crown, with great glory for those who have not stumbled.

**15:4** For I make no reckoning of the long-suffering of this world, save only where it brings righteousness. And those who have not loved my law and who have not understood the ways of the Most High will receive no profit.

**15:5** But those who have loved me, who have endured in my ways, and who have not set their life on the present world but who have set their soul on the world to come — these shall receive that which was promised.

**15:6** For if they are troubled now, that they may be glorified then — for great sorrow shall produce great glory.

**15:7** For as regards the righteous, they shall truly bear witness that they have suffered tribulation.

**15:8** And it shall appear in the end, and none shall be removed from the presence of the Most High, and their time shall not fail."

---

*SOPHIA notes: LOGOS base throughout. V.6 "great sorrow shall produce great glory" is the theological heart of the chapter — preserved verbatim from LOGOS. "Crown" (v.3) preserved as the eschatological reward image. "Long-suffering" (v.4) preserved for its theological precision.*
